title: Moving elements with translate vs with left
claim: Gameface RAG 07-performance.md, 'Transform vs. Layout: Animate Only What's Cheap' (SEVERITY: critical), which names this exact scenario: 'Animating floating damage numbers via top: 0 -> -5rem triggers a full Yoga solve every frame. Animating transform: translateY(0) -> translateY(-5rem) does not.' This case is the measurement behind that sentence.
result: CONFIRMED in the strongest available form: Layout is B-only at every count - animating left does not merely cost MORE layout than a transform, it introduces a Layout phase the transform variant never runs at all. The mirror image sits in the other column: UpdateNodeTransforms is A-only, because only the transform variant walks the scene graph. The two techniques do not differ in degree, they use different machinery. Script slightly favours B (0.89x / 0.77x), since writing style.left is one numeric assignment against building a translateX string - a real but small counterweight.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. transform/translateX are supported css-functions; left is supported with px units. Rule 1: one variable, the property used to move the element. Rule 2: identical DOM and identical CSS. Rule 3: identical JS apart from the single USE_TRANSFORM constant; both pages define both movement paths and both build the baseLeft array, so neither carries work the other lacks. Rule 4: no text, no assets. Rule 5: movers are 56x40 on a 92x68 grid and travel +/-16px, so at 300 elements everything stays inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: the movement IS the case and replaces the shared damage driver; fixed rAF rate from load in both. Rule 7: the offset derives from the frame counter and the element index. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is Layout - B should move Layout, A should not.
